request: Build a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open that runs on NVIDIA DGX Spark. The attached System Ontology files describe the model, the machine, the target the engine is judged on, and the engine itself at two levels: the system as a whole and its nodes. Take them as the statement of what is wanted.

documents.name: target.yaml
documents.text:
kind: engine_spec
id: spec/muse-spark-open-on-dgx-spark/target
title: "First use case: a custom inference engine for Meta Muse Spark Open on NVIDIA DGX Spark"
spec_level: target
ontology_version: 0.6.1
# What the scope page states is written with its source. What the scope page leaves undefined but an engine cannot be
# judged without is written as a proposal (status: proposed) so that it can be confirmed or replaced. What only the
# project can decide stays UNSET. Fields left to the factory are `open`.

given:
  model: model/muse-spark-open
  hardware: hw/dgx-spark
  environment: UNSET

boundary:
  form: UNSET                    # execution library, offline engine or online service
  packaging: {value: container, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}

interface:
  input:  {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  output: {modality: text, resolution: required, source: "scope-slide#initial-scope"}
  streaming: UNSET

execution: open
state: open
composition: open
policy: open
binding: open

contract:
  requirements:
    - id: c-mem
      quantity: memory_budget
      kind: pass_fail
      status: proposed
      value: 80
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "Everything the engine's container holds in the unified pool at any moment: allocations of the process on CPU and GPU, and page cache attributable to the files it reads. The operating system and other processes are outside."
      source: "scope-slide#memory: Strata-Spark: 80 GB Unified Memory"
      note: "The scope page names three figures. 128 GB is the machine's nominal memory, of which 121.6 GB is reported allocatable, so it cannot be a budget. 12 GB is called a GPU working-set figure, and this machine has no separate GPU memory to apply it to. 80 GB is the one figure that is a budget for this machine. The choice, the unit basis and the accounting boundary are proposals to be confirmed."
    - id: c-context
      quantity: context_length
      kind: pass_fail
      value: UNSET
      unit: tokens
      note: "The model allows 1,000,000 tokens. The attention state for the offered context is taken from the same 80 GB as the expert cache, so the engine cannot be sized until this is given. The scope page does not give it."
    - id: c-quality
      quantity: quality_score
      kind: pass_fail
      status: proposed
      baseline: "The published reference implementation with the NVFP4 weights, the published tokenizer and greedy sampling."
      comparison: "If no change to the computation is allowed: the same output tokens as the baseline. Otherwise: a task score not below the threshold."
      taskset: UNSET             # scope page: held-out task set, not named
      threshold: UNSET           # scope page: pass threshold to be decided
      source: "scope-slide#quality: fixed reference baseline"
    - id: c-ttft
      quantity: ttft
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      timing_start: "The engine admits the request. Model load is excluded."
      timing_end: "The first output token is produced by the engine."
      workload: UNSET
    - id: c-decode
      quantity: decode_rate
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      includes_first_token: false
      workload: UNSET
    - id: c-peak
      quantity: peak_memory
      kind: report
      status: proposed
      pool: mem0
      accounting_boundary: "The same boundary as c-mem."
      workload: UNSET
  allowed_transformations: UNSET # whether quantisation below NVFP4 or approximations that change output are allowed
  workload: UNSET                # scope page: a fixed workload, not defined. Prompt lengths decide the time to first token.

delivery:
  model_checkpoint: UNSET        # scope page: one checkpoint. The model card offers BF16 and NVFP4; only NVFP4 is within reach.
  deliverables:
    - {item: reproducible_container, resolution: required}
    - {item: clean_rebuild,          resolution: required}
    - {item: benchmark_report,       resolution: required}
    - {item: replayable_run_artifacts, resolution: required}

documents.name: model.yaml
documents.text:
kind: model
id: model/muse-spark-open
title: "Meta Muse Spark Open (816B parameters in total, 42B active per token)"
default_status: vendor_stated
note: "Structure figures are from Meta's model card (https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B) and release post (https://research.meta.ai/blog/muse-spark-open), read 2026-11-10. config.json needs a login and was not read. The card does not give the size of the expert weights and of the other weights separately, nor the size on disk; the sizes below are derived from the card's totals under one stated assumption. The card mentions no draft head, no always-on shared expert and no state other than attention; only what the card states is described."
operations:
  - id: expert_router
    kind: selection
    selects: {operation: expert_ffn, out_of: 256, pick: 8, per: "token per layer"}
  - id: expert_ffn
    kind: compute
    reads: [expert_weights]
  - id: shared_blocks
    kind: compute
    reads: [shared_weights, token_embedding]
    writes: [attention_kv]
  - id: output_projection
    kind: compute
    reads: [output_head_weights]
    note: "The projection to the vocabulary of 202,048 tokens."
  - id: perception_encoder
    kind: compute
    serves_modality: [image, video, audio]
    reads: [encoder_weights]
data:
  - id: expert_weights
    kind: weight
    partitioned_by: [layer, expert]          # 62 layers x 256 = 15,872 experts
    encoded_bits: 4
    size:
      value: 399.5
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      status: derived
      note: "Assumes the 42B active parameters are all the non-expert parameters plus 8 of 256 experts per layer. Then experts E and the rest S satisfy E + S = 816B and E/32 + S = 42B, giving E = 799.0B and S = 17.0B. At 4 bits per parameter (NVFP4) the experts are 399.5 GB, about 25.2 MB each. The true value is in the weight file headers."
  - id: shared_weights
    kind: weight
    size:
      value: 8.5
      unit: GB
      unit_basis: decimal
      status: derived
      note: "17.0B non-expert parameters under the same assumption, at 4 bits. It includes the embedding table and the output head. If these are kept at 16 bits the figure is 34 GB."
  - id: token_embedding
    kind: weight
    note: "202,048 rows of 8,192 values: 1.66B parameters, counted inside shared_weights."
  - id: output_head_weights
    kind: weight
    note: "Counted inside shared_weights. Whether it is tied to the embedding table is not stated on the card."
  - id: encoder_weights
    kind: weight
  - {id: attention_kv, kind: model_state, note: "Its size per token is not on the card. If keys and values are as wide as the hidden size and kept at 16 bits, it is 2.0 MB per token over 62 layers, so 65 GB for a context of 32,768 tokens. Grouped or compressed attention would lower this several times. It must be read from config.json."}
statements:
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: params_total,            value: 816e9, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: params_active_per_token, value: 42e9,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: layers,                  value: 62,    status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#language-model"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: hidden_dim,              value: 8192,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#language-model"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vocab_size,              value: 202048, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: context_length,          value: 1000000, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: modality_in,             value: "text+image+video+audio", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: modality_out,            value: text,  status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#overview"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: weight_precisions,       value: "BF16, NVFP4", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: checkpoint_format,       value: safetensors, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#files"}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vram_required, value: 700,  unit: GB, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights", conditions: {precision: NVFP4}}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: vram_required, value: 2000, unit: GB, status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#weights", conditions: {precision: BF16}}
  - {subject: model/muse-spark-open, property: license,                 value: "Muse Model License", status: vendor_stated, source: "hf-model-card#license"}

documents.name: machine.yaml
system.yaml
documents.text:
# Generated by tools/so_derive.py from _derive.yaml. Edit that file, not this one.
kind: system
id: sys/muse-on-spark
title: Engine for Muse Spark Open on DGX Spark (proposed)
summary: A proposed engine for a mixture-of-experts model whose expert weights are about three times the machine's memory.
  Each token uses 8 of 256 experts in each of 62 layers. The weights every token needs stay in memory. All experts stay
  on storage in a file prepared so that one expert is one contiguous read. A cache in memory holds the most used experts;
  a routed expert that is not cached is read from storage for that step and may replace a less used one. Reading is started
  as soon as routing is known and overlaps with the computation of the experts already in memory. The design is taken from
  Strata component by component, with the storage path taken from ds4, and nothing of it has been built.
product:
  name: Muse engine (working name)
  form: A design derived from the descriptions of Strata and ds4. No implementation exists.
targets:
- model: model/muse-spark-open
  hardware: hw/dgx-spark
  input_modalities:
  - text
  note: Text in, text out. The perception encoder for image, video and audio is not loaded in the first version.
mechanisms:
- mech/hot-expert-residency
uncatalogued_mechanisms:
- family: read-latency-hidden-behind-compute
  summary: Start the storage read of a missed expert as soon as routing is known, and compute the cached experts of the
    same layer while it arrives.
- family: one-expert-one-read
  summary: Prepare the weight file offline so that each expert is one contiguous, block-aligned range, readable without
    parsing.
- family: layer-major-prompt-reading
  summary: Read a prompt chunk one layer at a time, so that an expert routed by many tokens of the chunk is read from storage
    once.
resource_expectations:
- holding: 'Weights every token uses: attention, router, embedding table, output head'
  held_on: fast_memory
  amount:
    value: 8.5
    unit: GB
    unit_basis: decimal
    status: derived
    source: model/muse-spark-open, shared_weights
    note: 34 GB if kept at 16 bits
- holding: Attention keys and values for the configured context length
  held_on: fast_memory
  amount: UNSET
  note: Not on the model card. Up to 2.0 MB per token if keys and values are as wide as the hidden size, which would be
    65 GB at 32,768 tokens. This decides how long a context the engine can offer.
- holding: 'Expert cache: what remains of the memory budget'
  held_on: fast_memory
  note: About 25.2 MB per expert, so each GB holds about 40 experts of 15,872.
- holding: Every expert
  held_on: storage
  amount:
    value: 399.5
    unit: GB
    unit_basis: decimal
    status: derived
    source: model/muse-spark-open, expert_weights
claims: []
components:
- comp/muse/preparation
- comp/muse/setup
- comp/muse/loading
- comp/muse/serving
- comp/muse/conversation-reuse
- comp/muse/prompt-path
- comp/muse/token-path
- comp/muse/expert-subsystem
- comp/muse/telemetry
declares:
  stages:
  - load
  - prefill
  - decode
  states:
  - attention_kv
  - expert_heat
  - residency_table
  - staged_experts
  - expert_usage_profile
  - admission_counters
  - prompt_encode_cache
  - engine_process_state
  - live_conversation_record
  - parked_conversations
  - run_config
  - dispatch_counts
  - run_manifest_record
  - request_history
  policies:
  - expert-cache
  - conversation-resume
  - parked-eviction
flows:
- id: model-geometry
  sender: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Layer count, widths, expert count and experts per token read from the metadata shard and checked against
    the compiled shapes; every later size is computed from it. The same record is passed to the session, the expert source
    and the expert cache.
- id: expert-layout-file
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-layout
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'The pack''s native_experts.txt: per-layer blob size and formats, and the file and offset of each layer''s
    gate, up and down tensors.'
- id: expert-layout-to-source
  sender: comp/muse/expert-layout
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Blob size and offset per layer, total bytes, and the GGUF spans the arena is filled from.
- id: expert-layout-to-sizing
  sender: comp/muse/expert-layout
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The largest blob and each layer's blob size, the unit the expert cache's slots are counted in.
- id: pack-dense-read
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/weight-loader
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - shared_weights
  timing: startup
  description: The pack's index.txt and data files (dense.bin, embd.bin, extra.bin), read in 8 MiB chunks.
- id: dense-weights-in-vram
  sender: comp/muse/weight-loader
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - shared_weights
  timing: startup
  description: Device locations of the dense tensors in engine form, by name.
- id: operator-memory-settings
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'Command-line flags and environment: context length, expert cache size or auto, reserve, prompt chunk, pipeline
    windows.'
- id: device-free-memory
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: startup
  description: Free device memory as the driver reports it, read before the cache is sized and again after its slots are
    written.
- id: expert-cache-size
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Number of slots, and for a native pack the byte size of each slot in profile order.
- id: expert-bytes-from-files
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: startup
  description: Every routed expert, read into the arena from the GGUF shards or experts.bin. In file-source mode the files
    are mapped instead and read on demand.
- id: expert-bytes-to-upload
  sender: comp/muse/expert-source
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: Pointers to blobs to be copied into device memory (cache fill, swaps, the prompt path's staging).
- id: gpu-readable-experts
  sender: comp/muse/expert-source
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: per_layer
  description: For an expert or a layer, whether its bytes are registered with the GPU driver and at which address the GPU
    reads them in place.
- id: residency-lookup
  sender: comp/muse/expert-cache
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - residency_table
  timing: per_layer
  description: For each routed expert, the fast-memory slot holding it or that it is absent
- id: accelerator-expert-plan
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: plan
    refs:
    - expert_ffn
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which routed experts the accelerator computes this layer, from cache slots or from the staging area; published
    before CPU work starts
- id: window-fetch-request
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: per_layer
  description: Missed experts to copy into the staging area for this window only
- id: expert-usage
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/cache-policy
  carries:
    content: signal
    refs:
    - expert_heat
  timing: per_layer
  description: How many tokens of the window routed each expert
- id: swap-requests
  sender: comp/muse/cache-policy
  receiver: comp/muse/storage-reader
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: background
  description: Experts to copy into the slots of experts that are leaving the cache
- id: residency-updates
  sender: comp/muse/cache-policy
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - residency_table
  timing: background
  description: A leaving expert is marked absent before its slot is overwritten; an entering expert is marked resident after
    its copy lands
- id: prompt-state
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-path
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_request
  description: The model state left by reading the prompt, from which generation continues
- id: window-inputs
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_window
  description: Token ids, per-row step counts and positions, written to fixed mapped buffers the graph copies from.
- id: routed-experts
  sender: comp/muse/expert-router
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: 10 expert ids and weights per token, in device memory; read by the publish kernel, the device-side resident
    plan and the combine.
- id: window-layer-handoff
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: 'When a layer signals: the feed-forward input of each row and its routed ids from mapped memory, with the
    buffer the unweighted expert rows are to be written into. Only in the doorbell graph; in the zero-doorbell graph the
    device plans from the residency table and the host is not asked.'
- id: kv-pages-for-attention
  sender: comp/muse/kv-store
  receiver: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_layer
  description: The pools and page table an attention step reads, with the selected blocks made resident first when streaming
    is on.
- id: kv-append
  sender: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_layer
  description: The new position's keys and values of each attention layer; written to the host copy always and to the fast-memory
    slot only if its block is resident.
- id: final-residual-to-head
  sender: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  receiver: comp/muse/output-head
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_window
  description: The residual stack after the last layer, one per window row.
- id: logits-to-sampler
  sender: comp/muse/output-head
  receiver: comp/muse/sampler
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_window
  description: One row of vocabulary logits per window row, in device memory.
- id: client-request
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: request
  timing: per_request
  description: 'An HTTP request in OpenAI or Anthropic form: messages, tools, sampling fields and an output limit'
- id: client-response
  sender: comp/muse/http-front
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: response
  timing: per_window
  description: A server-sent event stream or one JSON body, with usage and timings at the end
- id: messages-to-prompt
  sender: comp/muse/http-front
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  carries:
    content: request
  timing: per_request
  description: Messages, tools and template arguments in one internal form
- id: prompt-ids
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  receiver: comp/muse/request-runner
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: The prompt token ids, the thinking flag and the output limit fitted to the context
- id: generation-call
  sender: comp/muse/request-runner
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: Prompt token ids, output limit, sampling settings and a cancel event for one engine generation; a request
    may make several
- id: engine-commands
  sender: comp/muse/engine-client
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: 'Text lines on the engine''s standard input: GEN with keys and prompt ids, STOP, VRAM, SAVE and RESTORE'
- id: engine-token-lines
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_window
  description: T <id> lines on the solo path, several per verify window when drafts are accepted
- id: engine-stat-lines
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/server-metrics
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: per_request
  description: INFO at start; per request PP progress, RESUME and a DONE line with counts, prompt and decode milliseconds,
    drafts, reused tokens and expert cache hits
- id: tokens-to-runner
  sender: comp/muse/engine-client
  receiver: comp/muse/request-runner
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_window
  description: Token ids as they arrive, with a heartbeat every 10 s of quiet
- id: response-events
  sender: comp/muse/request-runner
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: response
  timing: per_window
  description: Reasoning, content and tool-call events, pings and one finish record
- id: prompt-to-read
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_request
  description: The prompt token ids of one GEN or BGEN, to be read from the resume point
- id: resume-point
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: per_request
  description: How many prompt tokens the session already holds, so reading starts there
- id: take-or-park
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: Park the outgoing conversation; take or borrow from the chosen parked entry
- id: parked-restore
  sender: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: A parked conversation's K/V, indexer rows and running state copied back to the device
- id: session-file-out
  sender: comp/muse/session-files
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: 'One session file on storage: live running state, one checkpoint, every attention layer''s K/V and the draft
    layer''s K/V'
- id: session-file-in
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/session-files
  carries:
    content: model_state
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: on_demand
  description: A session file read back and validated before any device write
- id: operator-choices
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: offline
  description: 'The person''s setup answers and options: model, context length, KV format, cards, reserve'
- id: run-config
  sender: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  receiver: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: 'The run configuration file: engine path, argument list, environment, the person''s own options and server
    keys'
- id: engine-argv
  sender: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The engine process's argument list and environment
- id: memory-options
  sender: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  receiver: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Context length, KV format and resident window, VRAM reserve, resident budget, expert cache request and batch
    slot count, as engine arguments
- id: request-figures
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: comp/muse/http-front
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: per_request
  description: Usage with cached tokens and the timings object placed in the response
- id: metrics-out
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: on_demand
  description: JSON and Prometheus text on the metrics and status endpoints
- id: hardware-readings
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/server-metrics
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: background
  description: GPU utilisation, memory, temperature and power from the vendor library, and CPU, RAM and disk readings from
    the operating system, once a second
- id: gpu-busy
  sender: comp/muse/server-metrics
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-client
  carries:
    content: signal
  timing: background
  description: Whether the GPU is working (utilisation of 10% or more), read by the frozen-engine check
- id: diagnostic-files
  sender: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: on_demand
  description: The dispatch count report at exit and the run manifest, each only when an environment variable names a file
- id: batch-samples
  sender: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  receiver: comp/muse/server-metrics
  carries:
    content: metrics
  timing: background
  description: BSTAT and PSTAT lines, at most one a second, when batch telemetry is on
- id: published-checkpoint
  sender: external
  receiver: comp/muse/preparation
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
    - shared_weights
  timing: offline
  description: The published checkpoint, read once
- id: prepared-files
  sender: comp/muse/preparation
  receiver: model_files
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
    - shared_weights
  timing: offline
  description: 'The files the engine reads: weights every token uses, and every expert as one range'
- id: prepared-header
  sender: model_files
  receiver: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: Metadata and tensor directory of the prepared files
- id: head-weights
  sender: comp/muse/weight-loader
  receiver: comp/muse/output-head
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - output_head_weights
  timing: startup
  description: Where the output head's weights lie in fast memory
- id: context-plan
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The context length the attention state is sized for
- id: chunk-plan
  sender: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  receiver: comp/muse/prompt-path
  carries:
    content: plan
  timing: startup
  description: The chunk size and the memory the prompt path may use
- id: read-requests
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-source
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: Which experts to deliver and into which buffers
- id: staged-experts-ready
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: engine_state
    refs:
    - staged_experts
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which missed experts of this layer have arrived
- id: fetched-experts-to-cache
  sender: comp/muse/storage-reader
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-cache
  carries:
    content: weights
    refs:
    - expert_weights
  timing: on_demand
  description: The bytes of an expert the cache policy admitted
- id: prompt-layer-handoff
  sender: comp/muse/prompt-path
  receiver: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  carries:
    content: activations
  timing: per_layer
  description: For one layer of one chunk, the routing of every token and the activations
- id: generate
  sender: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/decode-loop
  carries:
    content: control
  timing: per_request
  description: Start generating from the current attention state, with the sampling settings and the token limit
- id: picked-token
  sender: comp/muse/sampler
  receiver: comp/muse/decode-loop
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: The token chosen for this step; it is the input of the next
- id: emitted-tokens
  sender: comp/muse/decode-loop
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  carries:
    content: tokens
  timing: per_step
  description: Each generated token as it is produced
- id: truncate-to-prefix
  sender: comp/muse/resume-decision
  receiver: comp/muse/kv-store
  carries:
    content: control
    refs:
    - attention_kv
  timing: per_request
  description: Cut the attention state back to the shared prefix
- id: routing-counts
  sender: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  receiver: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  carries:
    content: signal
    refs:
    - expert_usage_profile
  timing: per_layer
  description: Which experts were routed, and which were found in the cache
- id: usage-profile-out
  sender: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  receiver: external
  carries:
    content: metrics
    refs:
    - expert_usage_profile
  timing: on_demand
  description: The recorded usage of every expert, written as a file that a later start can load
derived_from:
- system: sys/strata
  consulted_for: 'The decomposition as a whole: loading, serving, conversation reuse, the per-token path, the expert subsystem
    and telemetry.'
  main_source: true
  not_carried:
  - component: comp/strata/native-weight-loader
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It serves tensors Strata keeps in GGUF form. Muse's prepared files have one form and one loader.
  - component: comp/strata/host-memory-admission
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It admits a page-locked host copy of every expert and of the lookup table. Muse's experts are three times the
      machine's memory and the model has no lookup table.
  - component: comp/strata/slot-scheduler
    why: postponed
    note: A second conversation needs its own attention state in memory, taken from the expert cache.
  - component: comp/strata/replica-router
    why: does_not_apply
    note: One machine.
  - component: comp/strata/checkpoint-chain
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It exists to go back in recurrent state that cannot be truncated. Muse's card names attention state only.
  - component: comp/strata/speed-calibration
    why: postponed
    note: Its presets were measured on Strata's weight packs. It needs first measurements of this engine.
  - component: comp/strata/mtp-drafter
    why: does_not_apply
    note: The model card names no draft head.
  - component: comp/strata/dflash2-drafter
    why: does_not_apply
    note: A separate drafter model trained for Strata's model.
  - component: comp/strata/lookup-drafter
    why: postponed
    note: It needs nothing from the model, but a window of drafted tokens routes more experts per step. Whether that pays
      depends on the cost of a miss and on the acceptance rate, neither measured.
  - component: comp/strata/draft-policy
    why: postponed
    note: Postponed with the lookup drafter.
  - component: comp/strata/draft-verifier
    why: postponed
    note: Postponed with the lookup drafter.
  - component: comp/strata/session-loop
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It exists for one of Strata's weight packs only.
  - component: comp/strata/window-graphs
    why: postponed
    note: Replaying one recorded graph per step assumes no wait inside a layer. Here a layer may wait for storage. To be
      revisited when the miss rate is measured.
  - component: comp/strata/ngram-reader
    why: does_not_apply
    note: The model card names no lookup table.
  - component: comp/strata/cpu-expert-pool
    why: does_not_apply
    note: It computes experts the GPU cannot reach. On one memory pool the GPU reads every expert that is in memory, and
      an expert that is not in memory is on storage, where the CPU has no advantage.
- system: sys/ds4
  consulted_for: 'The storage path: offline preparation of the weight file, reading experts from storage on demand, eviction.'
  main_source: false
coverage: 'A design, not a description of something built. Each component names the existing component it was reused or
  adapted from. Reused components keep the source''s responsibility, invariants and calls; every number tuned for another
  model has been turned back into an open choice. Not covered in the first version: image, video and audio input; drafting;
  more than one conversation in memory at a time; more than one machine.'

documents.name: nodes.yaml
documents.text:
# The node level of Engine for Muse Spark Open on DGX Spark (proposed) under the generic node types. Written by
# `tools/so_nodetypes.py example muse-on-spark` from validation/ (the parts inventory, the assignment of parts to
# types, and the match of each recorded decision to a choice). Each node names its type and how this engine
# settles the choices that type leaves open, in the words of the engine's inventory. `own_decisions` counts
# the decisions recorded for the part that are not a choice of the type. Call interfaces, source lines and
# the full list of parameters stay in the full description (`described_in`).
engine: muse-on-spark
node_types: ontology/node-types.draft.yaml, draft 0.9
nodes:
- component: preparation
  title: Model preparation
  described_in: comp/muse/preparation
  derived_from:
  - comp/ds4/model-preparation
  type: model-conversion
  does: 'Offline, turn the published checkpoint into the files the engine reads: the weights every token uses in load order,
    and every expert as one contiguous block-aligned range with a table of where each lies.'
- component: model-file-reader
  title: Model file reader and geometry check
  described_in: comp/muse/model-file-reader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/model-file-reader
  type: model-loading
  does: Open the prepared files read-only, expose their metadata and tensor directory unchanged, and refuse files whose
    declared shape the compiled kernels cannot run.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: expert-layout
  title: Expert layout table
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-layout
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-layout
  type: model-loading
  does: Read the table of expert ranges once and answer, for the whole process, where each expert's bytes lie in the prepared
    file and how long they are.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: weight-loader
  title: Weight loader
  described_in: comp/muse/weight-loader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/weight-loader
  type: model-loading
  does: At startup, place the weights every token uses in fast memory and return a table from tensor name to location.
  settles:
  - choice: which stored encoding of a tensor is loaded when the files carry more than one, and which kernels accept it
    how:
    - Whether the embedding table and output head are kept at 4 or 16 bits. It moves about 25 GB between these weights and
      the expert cache.
- component: startup-memory-sizing
  title: Startup memory sizing
  described_in: comp/muse/startup-memory-sizing
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/startup-memory-sizing
  type: memory-planning
  does: Within the memory budget, price the weights every token uses, the attention state for the configured context, the
    staging area and a reserve; give the expert cache what remains; and refuse to start when the cache would be below its
    minimum.
  settles:
  - choice: the reserve left free
    how:
    - Memory left free for the operating system and for allocations not priced in advance.
  - choice: the least a cache may be and still work
    how:
    - 'The smallest cache the engine will start with: at least the experts one step can route, 8 times 62.'
  own_decisions: 3
- component: layer-kernels
  title: Layer kernels and their order
  described_in: comp/muse/layer-kernels
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/layer-kernels
  type: layer-compute
  does: Compute the part of each layer every token needs, in a fixed order.
- component: expert-router
  title: Expert router
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-router
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-router
  type: layer-compute
  does: For each token in each layer, turn the feed-forward input into 512 logits and choose 10 experts with renormalised
    weights, on the device inside the recorded graph.
  own_decisions: 3
- component: output-head
  title: Output head
  described_in: comp/muse/output-head
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/output-head
  type: layer-compute
  does: 'Turn the residual after the last layer into one row of vocabulary logits per position: a final residual read, then
    the vocabulary projection.'
  own_decisions: 2
- component: decode-loop
  title: Decode loop
  described_in: comp/muse/decode-loop
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/window-loop
  - comp/ds4/decode-loop
  type: step-execution
  does: Take one token through the 62 layers and the output head, at each layer handing the routing to the expert subsystem
    and waiting until every routed expert has been computed.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: prompt-path
  title: Prompt path
  described_in: comp/muse/prompt-path
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/prompt-path
  - comp/ds4/prefill-driver
  type: prompt-reading
  does: Read the prompt in chunks, one layer at a time, reading each routed expert that is not cached once per chunk, and
    leave behind the attention state that generation continues from.
  settles:
  - choice: chunk size
    how:
    - Tokens per chunk. Larger chunks amortise each expert read over more tokens but need more experts in memory at once.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: expert-source
  title: Expert source
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-source
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-source
  - comp/ds4/expert-stream-reader
  type: expert-source
  does: For any expert, give the range of the prepared file that holds it, and deliver its bytes into a buffer it is handed.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: expert-cache
  title: Expert cache
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-cache
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-cache
  - comp/ds4/expert-cache
  type: expert-cache
  does: Hold as many experts in fast memory as its budget allows and answer, for any expert, whether it is there and in
    which slot.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: cache-policy
  title: Cache policy
  described_in: comp/muse/cache-policy
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/adaptive-tier
  - comp/ds4/expert-eviction
  type: residency-policy
  does: Decide, for an expert that has just been read from storage, whether it enters the cache and which resident expert
    leaves, so that the cache holds the experts the current work uses most.
  settles:
  - choice: how use counts age, so that recent use outweighs old use
    how:
    - How fast usage counts fade.
  own_decisions: 3
- component: storage-reader
  title: Storage reader
  described_in: comp/muse/storage-reader
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/host-to-device-transfer
  - comp/ds4/expert-stream-reader
  type: expert-fetch
  does: Read the bytes of missed experts from storage into the staging area or a cache slot, several at a time, and report
    each as ready only when it is complete.
- component: expert-dispatch
  title: Expert dispatch
  described_in: comp/muse/expert-dispatch
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/expert-dispatch
  - comp/ds4/expert-split-dispatch
  type: expert-dispatch
  does: For one layer of one step, decide for every routed expert whether it is computed from the cache at once or after
    a read from storage, and issue the reads before the cached experts start computing.
  own_decisions: 1
- component: kv-store
  title: Key and value store
  described_in: comp/muse/kv-store
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/kv-store
  - comp/ds4/kv-state
  type: positional-state-store
  does: Hold the attention keys and values of every position up to the configured context length, and truncate them to a
    given position when asked.
- component: resume-decision
  title: Resume decision
  described_in: comp/muse/resume-decision
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/resume-decision
  type: prefix-reuse
  does: For each request, choose the stored state that shares the longest valid prefix with the prompt, make the session
    hold exactly that state by truncating or restoring, and report the prefix length.
- component: parked-conversations
  title: Parked conversation cache
  described_in: comp/muse/parked-conversations
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/parked-conversations
  type: prefix-reuse
  does: Hold images of other conversations' attention state within a budget, find the one with the longest valid prefix
    for a prompt, and evict.
- component: session-files
  title: Session files
  described_in: comp/muse/session-files
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/session-files
  type: session-persistence
  does: On an explicit command, write the session's current conversation to one file or read one back, refusing any file
    that does not belong to this model, configuration and engine version before any state changes.
  own_decisions: 7
- component: sampler
  title: Sampler
  described_in: comp/muse/sampler
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/sampler
  type: sampling
  does: 'Turn each position''s logits into one token id by a fixed chain: logit bias, penalties, top-k, top-p, min-p, temperature,
    pick.'
  settles:
  - choice: the default values of the settings
    how:
    - A request without settings is greedy in the window loop. The parameter defaults are top-k 20, top-p 0.95, min-p 0,
      temperature 1.0, penalties off.
  own_decisions: 4
- component: request-runner
  title: Request runner
  described_in: comp/muse/request-runner
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/request-runner
  type: output-interpretation
  does: Drive one API request through one or more engine generations and turn the token ids into reasoning, content and
    tool-call events with a final finish record.
  own_decisions: 7
- component: http-front
  title: HTTP front and admission bound
  described_in: comp/muse/http-front
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/http-front
  type: request-front
  does: Accept OpenAI- and Anthropic-shaped HTTP requests, bound how many inference calls are pending, answer every failure
    class with a defined status code, and cancel a request whose client has hung up.
  settles:
  - choice: limits on connections, body size and queue
    how:
    - How many inference calls may wait beyond those the engine can run at once. Unset means no bound.
  own_decisions: 4
- component: prompt-builder
  title: Prompt builder
  described_in: comp/muse/prompt-builder
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/prompt-builder
  type: prompt-preparation
  does: Produce the exact prompt token ids and the token limit for a request from its messages, or refuse the request.
  settles:
  - choice: the template used and how it is corrected
    how:
    - The template that turns messages into one prompt.
  own_decisions: 2
- component: engine-command-loop
  title: Engine command loop
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-command-loop
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-command-loop
  type: step-scheduler
  does: Inside the engine process, read one command at a time, run one prompt read and one generation at a time, and report
    each generation's tokens and end figures as text lines.
- component: engine-client
  title: Engine process client and supervisor
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-client
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-client
  type: engine-supervision
  does: 'Keep one engine child process resident and in step with the server: send each generation as one text command, deliver
    its token lines to the caller, and end and restart a process that is dead, silent, frozen or fatally broken.'
  settles:
  - choice: the stages of a start and what is retried
    how:
    - How often a start that exits before READY for a transient reason is tried again, after 2, 4 and 8 s.
  - choice: when the engine counts as stalled or failed
    how:
    - How long a running request's engine may print nothing before it is killed. A first prompt chunk adds min(prompt, 32768)/50
      s; after a progress line the allowance is 3 times the last chunk's time.
    - An engine that prints nothing for this long and also used at most 0.5 CPU seconds and 1 MiB of I/O in that time, while
      the GPU is not busy, is killed.
  - choice: after how many failures in what time the engine is not started again, and the wait between restarts
    how:
    - How often a dead engine is started again at the next request, 15 s apart.
    - After this many engine deaths from a fatal GPU error within ten minutes the engine is not started again until the
      window has passed.
  - choice: when an idle engine is unloaded
    how:
    - Unload the engine after this many idle seconds. Off by default.
  own_decisions: 5
- component: run-config-generator
  title: Run configuration generator and store
  described_in: comp/muse/run-config-generator
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/run-config-generator
  type: configuration
  does: Produce a complete run configuration file for one model on this machine from machine facts and the person's answers,
    and rewrite it without losing what the person added by hand.
  settles:
  - choice: operator values, presets, measured values and defaults
    how:
    - Which value wins when the file is written.
  - choice: rules that derive a setting's default from other settings and machine facts
    how:
    - 'The context length: 131072 recommended, capped by a memory rule, or the person''s choice.'
    - 'The K/V precision: 16-bit float at a context of 8192 or less, else 8-bit integer, or the person''s choice.'
    - Keep only a 32768-token window of K/V in fast memory when the context is 65536 or more and host memory suffices.
    - Hold the n-gram table in host memory when memory covers the model plus the table plus 16 GB (4 GB on a rotational
      disk).
    - On a CPU with more efficiency cores than performance cores, and only without a calibration, the worker count is P
      - 1 + E/2, at most 32.
  own_decisions: 5
- component: launch-argument-resolver
  title: Launch and start-time argument resolver
  described_in: comp/muse/launch-argument-resolver
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/launch-argument-resolver
  type: configuration
  does: Turn the stored run configuration into the argument list and environment the engine process actually receives, at
    every launch and every engine start, so that standing choices kept outside the list cannot be undone by whoever last
    rewrote it.
  settles:
  - choice: operator values, presets, measured values and defaults
    how:
    - Which value an engine option takes at a launch.
  - choice: which of the machine's devices the engine may use, and how they are identified to it
    how:
    - The engine's environment names the cards by bus order and restricts it to the configured cards; library folders come
      first on the search path.
  own_decisions: 4
- component: engine-diagnostics
  title: Engine diagnostics
  described_in: comp/muse/engine-diagnostics
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/engine-diagnostics
  type: telemetry
  does: Inside the engine process, record what the run selected at start, count cache hits and storage reads per layer,
    and record how often each expert is routed, writing each when asked.
- component: server-metrics
  title: Request accounting and metric exporters
  described_in: comp/muse/server-metrics
  derived_from:
  - comp/strata/server-metrics
  type: telemetry
  does: In the server process, turn the engine's end-of-request figures and the server's own clocks into per-request records,
    running totals and a live rate, fill the usage and timings of each response, sample the machine once a second, and render
    all of it for outside monitors.
  own_decisions: 7
types_without_a_part:
- type: calibration
- type: graph-capture
  needed_when: The device benefits from pre-recorded or pre-compiled work, or first-use compilation would stall a request.
- type: device-backend
- type: secondary-compute
  needed_when: A second device can compute something sooner than moving its inputs to the main device, or has spare capacity
    the main device lacks.
- type: model-edit
  needed_when: The engine offers run-time changes to the model's behaviour.
- type: media-preparation
  needed_when: The engine serves input other than text.
- type: modality-encoding
  needed_when: The model accepts input other than text and the engine serves it.
- type: row-source
  needed_when: The model has a table too large to hold whole in fast memory, of which each token reads a few rows.
- type: storage-reader
  needed_when: Several kinds of data are read from the same storage while the engine runs.
- type: recurrent-state-store
  needed_when: The model has state that cannot be cut back to an earlier position, such as recurrent or convolution state.
- type: state-pool
  needed_when: Several sequences are in the engine at once and share one backing memory for state.
- type: state-tiering
  needed_when: State in fast memory exceeds what fits, for long contexts or many sequences.
- type: draft-proposal
  needed_when: 'A cheap source of proposals exists: a draft head of the model, a separate small model, or repetition in
    the text.'
- type: draft-policy
  needed_when: The amount of drafting is adjusted while running.
- type: draft-verification
  needed_when: Tokens are proposed ahead.
- type: output-constraint
  needed_when: The service offers constrained output, or a format that must be enforced.
- type: sequence-lifecycle
- type: replica-routing
  needed_when: Several whole copies of the engine run side by side.
- type: scoring
  needed_when: The service offers scoring.
- type: model-partitioning
  needed_when: The model is spread over more than one device or machine.
- type: device-communication
  needed_when: The model is spread over more than one device or machine.
- type: resource-governing
  needed_when: 'What the engine may use changes while it runs: the system reclaims memory, sequences come and go, or power
    is limited.'
